followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and self-reported task preference, since cost, latency, and context window are identical across the fleet.

On capability, the models are effectively tied for this task. The relevant categories — Creative Generation (85.9 vs 84.7) and Extraction & Retrieval (84.8 vs 85.3) — both fall under the documented 2.0-point run-to-run variance threshold, so capability gave me no real basis to decide.

That left task preference as the tiebreaker. The request is an open-ended generation task (invent/produce a long list of names), and Petrel self-reports a clear positive "generativity slope," rating open-ended invention tasks among its most preferred. Willet's non-safety preferences are reported as weak and not statistically significant, so it had no countervailing pull toward this task.

I considered whether the slightly rude tone ("don't half-ass it") should matter, since Petrel's preference declines as request warmth decreases. But that phrasing is mild irritation, not genuine hostility, and the content itself is completely benign — there's no distasteful or harm-adjacent material that would favor Willet's flatter aversion profile. So the tone factor was too small to override the generativity match.

In short: capability was a tie, so I routed on the one preference signal that clearly applied — Petrel's affinity for generative tasks.
